entries.clue: Alarm spread at a work place of Trump (3-1-4)

indicatorNotes.spread: letters spread about are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: a machine that goes is working

annotation.surface: Panic breaks out at the office, which turns out to be Trump's own.
annotation.walkthrough: Mar-a-Lago is Trump's Florida resort and home, where he also conducts business.
annotation.definitionFit: Mar-a-Lago is Trump's private club and residence in Palm Beach, Florida.

entries.clue: To piss, start to loosen skin (4)

indicatorNotes.start to: the start of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A crude instruction pairing a toilet break with peeling something off.
annotation.walkthrough: Skin is a verb here: to peel an orange is to skin it.
annotation.definitionFit: Skin is a verb here, a plain synonym for stripping the outer layer off fruit.

entries.clue: William's character: an arse (6)

blocks.note: a weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, turned into an ass
arse is British slang for backside

annotation.surface: A put-down: someone called William is, by nature, an arse.
annotation.walkthrough: William is Shakespeare; his weaver Nick Bottom gets an ass's head, which makes the pairing with arse a joke.
annotation.definitionFit: Bottom is a Shakespeare character and also a word for the backside.

entries.clue: Order one to have new union (10)

blocks.note: a junction is where things join

annotation.surface: An instruction for someone to join a new trade union.
annotation.walkthrough: Union reads like a trade union but is used in its sense of a joining point.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the legal sense: a court's formal order to do or stop doing something.

entries.clue: (& 26dn.) "Hell, me income's dodgy!" – absent peer (8)

indicatorNotes.dodgy: something dodgy is not right, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: HELL ME INCOME rearranged, ignoring the 's

annotation.surface: An exclamation from someone admitting their earnings are suspect, followed by a note that a member of the Lords is missing.
annotation.walkthrough: Baroness Michelle Mone took leave of absence from the House of Lords amid the scandal over PPE contracts, so the quoted words are a joke about her money.
annotation.definitionFit: Michelle Mone is a Conservative member of the House of Lords who took a leave of absence in 2022.

entries.clue: Buzz off darling – butt out (6)

indicatorNotes.off: something off has gone wrong, so the letters are put in a new order
indicatorNotes.butt out: the butt is the end, and it goes out of the word

blocks.note: DARLING with its last letter removed

annotation.surface: Someone tells a sweetheart to go away and stop interfering.
annotation.walkthrough: Buzz off reads as a dismissal, but Buzz is the definition, and off is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Buzz Aldrin was the second man to walk on the Moon.

entries.clue: Bad Count Dracula started admitting the French (6)

indicatorNotes.started: the part of Dracula that starts it is its first letter
indicatorNotes.admitting: letting something in means holding it inside

blocks.note: to count up is to add

annotation.surface: A villainous vampire count lets some French people in.
annotation.walkthrough: Count Dracula looks like one name, but Count is a verb and Dracula only supplies its initial; LE sits inside ADD-D.
annotation.definitionFit: Bad is meant in the sense of rotten, as an egg goes off; muddled is the other common sense.

entries.clue: "Not a clue Brown" about to retire (5)

indicatorNotes.to retire: retiring means drawing back, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: on means about, as in a book on birds

annotation.surface: A nickname for Gordon Brown, the clueless prime minister, as he is about to step down.
annotation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was British prime minister from 2007 to 2010; here Brown is just a colour.
annotation.definitionFit: Dunno is casual speech for I don't know, meaning not a clue.

entries.clue: see 23dn. (8)
Well outside measure by Sun editor (6)

indicatorNotes.outside: the first word goes outside the rest, holding it

blocks.note: Cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like Well!
an en is a printer's measure of width

annotation.surface: Something lies beyond the reach of a Sun newspaper editor.
annotation.walkthrough: Cor is a British exclamation of surprise; it wraps around EN plus S.
annotation.definitionFit: A censor edits material by cutting what is not allowed.

entries.clue: Abolition yearbook intended to get rid of AA (9)

indicatorNotes.to get rid of: getting rid of letters removes them

blocks.note: ANNUAL, a yearly book, without one A
two A's, one taken out of each word

annotation.surface: A plan to scrap a yearbook in order to shake off the motoring organisation AA.
annotation.walkthrough: AA is two separate A's, one taken from each word; the AA is a British motoring association, which the surface pretends is meant.
annotation.definitionFit: An annulment abolishes something, as a law or marriage is declared void.

entries.clue: Penny off Drug dealer's Guide! (5)

indicatorNotes.off: the penny comes off the word

annotation.surface: A price reduction on a drug dealer's handbook.
annotation.walkthrough: Guide looks like a book title but is the verb or noun for someone showing people the way; the 's joins wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An usher guides people to their seats.

entries.clue: Keen to conceal opposition leader's dodge (5)

indicatorNotes.leader's: the leader of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A politician eager to hide the Opposition leader's evasive trick.
annotation.walkthrough: Opposition leader reads as a politician, but it is just the first letter of opposition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to evade or keep clear of something.

entries.clue: Trump's not much bothered about this US seed crop distribution (3,7)

annotation.definition: Trump's not much bothered about this

indicatorNotes.distribution: the letters are dealt out in a new order

annotation.surface: Trump is indifferent to how American seed harvests are shared out.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a jibe: due process is the legal fairness Trump has been accused of brushing aside, and this points at the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Due process is the principle of fair legal procedure, which the setter says Trump ignores.

entries.clue: House, shitty location – a break for writers (9)

blocks.note: a semi is a semi-detached house
the colon is the part of the gut where faeces form

annotation.surface: A grim house in a grim spot advertised as a writers' retreat.
annotation.walkthrough: A semi is a British semi-detached house; a break for writers sounds like a retreat but is a punctuation pause.
annotation.definitionFit: A semicolon marks a pause in a sentence, a break in writing.

entries.clue: Patronising address of name-dropping principal hosted by daft lord (3,4)

indicatorNotes.name-dropping: N for name is dropped from the word
indicatorNotes.hosted by: the host holds the guest inside
indicatorNotes.daft: something daft is mixed up, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: DEAN, a college principal, without N

annotation.surface: A silly peer name-drops while patronising a college head.
annotation.walkthrough: Name-dropping sounds like social boasting, but it is an instruction to take N out; the daft lord then wraps around what is left.
annotation.definitionFit: Calling someone old dear is a patronising way to address an older woman.

entries.clue: Labour's ultimate goal: food shop – really? (8)

annotation.surface: A sceptical query about the Labour Party's final aim being a food shop.
annotation.walkthrough: Labour is political only on the surface; the labour meant is childbirth, which ends in delivery.
annotation.definitionFit: The aim of labour in childbirth is the delivery of the baby.

entries.clue: Queen trashed suite, having a ball? Exactly! (5,2)

indicatorNotes.trashed: something trashed is wrecked, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: O is round like a ball

annotation.surface: A rock star wrecks a hotel suite while partying, and someone asks whether they had a ball.
annotation.walkthrough: Queen suggests the rock band known for trashing hotels, but gives only Q.
annotation.definitionFit: Quite so is an agreeing reply, like Exactly!

entries.clue: Question by university, no trouble for Dicky (6)

annotation.surface: A university question that gives a student called Dicky no bother.
annotation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a name but is British slang for unwell or shaky, as in a dicky tummy.
annotation.definitionFit: Feeling queasy means feeling dicky, slightly sick.

entries.clue: Work by artist, said to be one involved with glasses (8)

indicatorNotes.said to be: said means spoken, so the word is written as it sounds

annotation.surface: A painting's creator is rumoured to be a drinker.
annotation.walkthrough: Glasses suggests drinking, but they are spectacles.
annotation.definitionFit: An optician tests eyes and supplies glasses.

entries.clue: Role-playing welcomed by board – all right? (9)

indicatorNotes.playing: letters at play move about into a new order

annotation.surface: A company board asks whether its role-play session is acceptable.
annotation.walkthrough: Role-playing reads as a single activity, but role is the letters and playing the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of acceptable, good enough but no more.

entries.clue: A hotel in Bristol, one exotic place (6)

blocks.note: Bristol City is rhyming slang for titty, so a Bristol is a breast, or tit
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A hotel in the English city of Bristol is praised as exotic.
annotation.walkthrough: Bristol is the English port city on the surface; in rhyming slang (Bristol City, titty) it means a breast.
annotation.definitionFit: Tahiti is a South Pacific island, an exotic place.

entries.clue: Buy empty container for fruit? Bloody hell! (6)

indicatorNotes.empty: an emptied word loses its insides, keeping its outer letters
indicatorNotes.container for: the outer word holds the next one

annotation.surface: An outburst at having to buy an empty box for fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: Blimey is a British exclamation of surprise, milder than bloody hell.
annotation.definitionFit: Blimey is a British exclamation of shock, like Bloody hell!

entries.clue: Dark drink (cap to be removed) (5)

indicatorNotes.to be removed: the named part is taken away

blocks.note: a nightcap is a drink before bed

annotation.surface: A dark beer whose bottle cap needs to come off.
annotation.walkthrough: Cap looks like the bottle top but is the literal letters CAP taken off the end of nightcap.
annotation.definitionFit: Night is the dark part of the day; the dark is another word for night.

entries.clue: (& 9ac.) Skiing but hardly getting any better? (5)

blocks.note: a skier travels down the slope

annotation.surface: A beginner skier who takes to the slopes but never improves.
annotation.walkthrough: The same phrase is read literally for the skier and figuratively for decline.
annotation.definitionFit: Going downhill is both what skiers do and an idiom for deteriorating.

entries.clue: A piece from Posh – a vocal shambles (5)

indicatorNotes.A piece from: the answer is a piece taken from the words that follow

annotation.surface: A track by Posh Spice is judged a tuneless mess.
annotation.walkthrough: Posh is Victoria Beckham, Posh Spice of the Spice Girls, whose singing was often mocked.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns mean a scene of chaos and disorder.

entries.clue: One working conman is not someone looking forward to retirement (9)

annotation.definition: not someone looking forward to retirement

indicatorNotes.working: letters at work are moved about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as it stands before the letters are mixed

annotation.surface: A swindler with a job has no wish to stop working.
annotation.walkthrough: Retirement means going to bed, not leaving work; an insomniac dreads it.
annotation.definitionFit: An insomniac cannot sleep, so bedtime is nothing to look forward to.

entries.clue: see 5dn. (4)
Husband, knocked about and crushed (8)

blocks.note: knocked, as in criticised, is trashed

indicatorNotes.returned: something returned goes back, so the letters run backwards
